_comment: Hard dollar cap for the FIRST real (non-zero-token) AI E2E run across the Research -> Script -> QC -> Correction -> Final Technical Check chain. Enforced by .github/scripts/preflight_budget_guard.py BEFORE each real provider call — never post-hoc. Pricing itself is never guessed here: the guard reads it from .github/config/cost-guard.json's monetary.price_registry, which must have an explicit entry for the exact provider:model pair below.

input_estimation._comment: No live tokenizer call is made before the real provider call — that would itself be a network call this preflight step must not make. Input tokens are instead estimated conservatively from the REAL prompt/system file about to be sent: chars / chars_per_token, then inflated by safety_margin. Deliberately biased to OVER-estimate (a false-positive fail-closed is safe; a false-negative that lets an over-budget call through is not).

research._comment: Input ceiling: scraped/aggregated source text has no other stage's max_model_output to bound it, so this is a deliberately generous standalone planning ceiling (~18000 chars / ~6000 true tokens) plus normal system/instruction overhead. Allocation covers (assumed_max_input_tokens * safety_margin) priced at max_model_output output — i.e. the guard's actual worst-case ESTIMATE, not the raw assumed token count.

script._comment: Input is the research issue's extracted top-3-ideas section only (not the full research body) — small by construction.

quality_control._comment: Input is bounded by the script stage's own max_model_output (4800) plus overhead.

correction._comment: Input is bounded by script's max_model_output (4800) + QC's max_model_output (4500) plus overhead.

final_technical_control._comment: Input is bounded by correction's max_model_output (4500) + QC's max_model_output (4500) plus overhead.
